compiled:
📰 General

Measles Cases Surge Dramatically in California, Particularly Among Young People •

California has experienced a significant increase in measles cases, with 52 confirmed cases reported in the first six and a half months of 2026. This represents a doubling of the 25 cases recorded throughout the entirety of 2025. The surge is concentrated among children and young adults, according to health officials. Experts attribute the rise to declining vaccination rates and a resurgence of the highly contagious disease.

🌍 World

Trump Considers Military Action in Mali Against JNIM Group •

President Donald Trump is reportedly exploring the possibility of launching military strikes within Mali. Advisers are evaluating potential action against al-Qaeda-linked group, Jama’at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). The focus of the potential intervention is centered on combating the group’s activities in the country. This consideration marks a potential expansion of U.S. military involvement beyond existing operations in the region. The White House has not yet confirmed the extent of these discussions.

🦅 US

Apple’s Next Macs Could Skip M5, Launching Directly with M6 •

According to a report from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is planning to release two new Mac models that will utilize the M6 chip directly. This strategy would bypass the M5 series, which is currently the base processor for many Apple products. Gurman’s report outlines a multi-year roadmap, suggesting a shift towards faster processor adoption within the Mac lineup. The move indicates Apple’s continued investment in developing its own silicon technology.

💰 Business

EU’s Google Fine Sparks Trump’s Retaliation Threat, Tariffs Loom •

The European Union’s recent €890 million fine against Google is fueling concerns that President Donald Trump will respond with further tariffs targeting U.S. tech companies. Sources indicate that the EU was aware of the potential for a negative reaction from Washington, anticipating criticism of previous fines levied against American tech giants. Trump has previously voiced strong opposition to these fines, arguing they are unfairly targeted. This situation raises the possibility of escalating trade tensions between the EU and the United States.

💻 Technology

OpenAI Expands ChatGPT Health Access to All U.S. Users Over 18 •

OpenAI announced today that ChatGPT Health, its AI-powered tool designed to answer health-related questions, is now accessible to all U.S. users aged 18 and older. Previously, the feature was limited to a select group of beta testers and specific plans. The company stated this expansion follows a recent lawsuit filed by a Florida-based pastor alleging concerns about the tool’s capabilities. OpenAI continues to refine ChatGPT Health based on user feedback and ongoing safety evaluations.

🎭 Entertainment

Mobile Suit Gundam RG-XARX-Zero Trailer Unveiled at San Diego Comic-Con •

Bandai Namco Filmworks revealed a new Mobile Suit Gundam series, titled RG-XARX-Zero, prior to its debut at San Diego Comic-Con. The trailer showcased the anime’s initial Mobile Suit designs and animation style. The series is being developed by the team behind the Rebuild of Mobile Suit Gundam films. Details regarding the plot and characters remain undisclosed at this time. The release date for Mobile Suit Gundam RG-XARX-Zero has not yet been announced.

🏅 Sports

Usman Questions Future After Devastating Loss to Du Plessis in UFC Fight •

Kamaru Usman suffered a dominant unanimous decision loss to Dricus du Plessis at UFC Oklahoma City. The fight saw du Plessis consistently land significant strikes and control the octagon, leading to a clear advantage for the challenger. Usman acknowledged the defeat as a “lopsided” loss, expressing uncertainty about his continued participation in the sport. Following the fight, Usman stated he is considering whether it is worth continuing to pursue a career in mixed martial arts. This defeat marks a significant downturn in Usman’s previously dominant UFC career.

🔬 Science

Scientists Identify Novel Biological State Bridging Life and Death Processes •

Researchers have identified a previously unrecognized state of biological activity occurring in organisms following clinical death. Studies involving zebrafish demonstrated sustained, albeit reduced, cellular function and gene expression after cessation of heartbeat and breathing. This “zombie” state involved the reactivation of certain cellular processes, including DNA repair and protein synthesis. The findings challenge the traditional understanding of death as a definitive endpoint and open new avenues for research into organ preservation and potential resuscitation techniques.

🩺 Health

Costa Rica Chikungunya Outbreak Triggers CDC Level 2 Travel Warning for Tourists •

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has issued a Level 2 travel warning for Costa Rica due to a rising outbreak of chikungunya. Cases of the mosquito-borne virus are increasing, prompting health officials to advise travelers to take enhanced preventative measures. The CDC’s warning indicates a moderate risk for travelers visiting the Central American nation. Officials are urging visitors to utilize insect repellent and take steps to avoid mosquito bites to minimize their risk of infection.
